## What Is an Enterprise Products Partners Internship?


An Enterprise Products Partners internship is an 11-week, paid summer placement at the company's corporate office in Houston, Texas. Enterprise is a master limited partnership (NYSE: EPD) and[one of the largest publicly traded partnerships in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enterprise_Products) , operating more than 50,000 miles of pipeline, over 300 million barrels of liquids storage and 14 billion cubic feet of natural gas storage. The company sits in the middle of the energy supply chain: gathering, treating, processing, transporting and storing natural gas, NGLs, crude oil, petrochemicals and refined products, plus running a marine transportation business on U.S. inland and intracoastal waterways. Interns join one of five focus areas and "learn from leading energy professionals in a challenging environment designed to enhance their skills in the workplace and classroom."


## When Do Enterprise Products Partners Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028?


Enterprise Products does not follow the conventional campus-recruiting calendar. There is no requisition to watch, no posting to wait for, and no published opening or closing date. The company's internship page gives one instruction: email campusrecruiting@eprod.com. Half of intern candidates on Glassdoor report reaching the company through campus recruiting events, so the practical timing is the autumn campus season for a following-summer start. But the email channel has no expiration, which means the right time to send is now.

The company's official careers page is always the most current source. If a role is posted there, go by that, even if this page suggests the window hasn't opened yet.*


### Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open


Enterprise Products does not have a rolling deadline because it does not have a deadline at all. The email address is always open, but campus recruiting is seasonal and the team reads the mailbox on its own schedule. Glassdoor shows intern interviews averaging 4 days from first contact to hire, which means once the recruiting team is active, decisions happen fast, and early emails are in the pile before the volume arrives. There is no second application to submit if you miss the first pass. The simplest thing you can do is email campusrecruiting@eprod.com this week with a resume and a transcript, name one of the five focus areas in the subject line, and reference a sub-discipline inside it. That puts you ahead of every candidate who is still looking for an apply button.

## Which Enterprise Products Partners Internship Programs Should You Target?


Enterprise publishes five internship focus areas, each with named sub-disciplines. The internship page is only about 120 words long, but those 34 named sub-disciplines are the most specific thing it publishes and the best tool for targeting your application.

Commercial & Distribution Asset Management, Business Development, Marketing & Logistics 11 weeks Paid; Houston corporate office


Engineering Process Engineering, Project Engineering, Operations, Asset Integrity, Mechanical & Electrical Reliability, Pipeline Systems Planning, Measurement, Process Controls, Environmental 11 weeks Paid; Houston corporate office


Information Technology Applications, Big Data Services, Business Solutions, Client Services, Infrastructure and Operations, Security and Compliance 11 weeks Paid; Houston corporate office

Name one focus area and one sub-discipline in your email. Writing "I am interested in your Volume Accounting or Regulatory Reporting work within Accounting & Risk Control" is specific in a way almost no cold email is, and it costs nothing.


## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


Enterprise publishes almost nothing about eligibility, which is itself a notable finding:


• **Student status:** the program is for "students interested in gaining hands-on experience in the energy industry," and a transcript is required with the application, confirming current enrollment.


• **Fields of study:** not stated as a formal list, but the five focus areas map to accounting, finance, tax, engineering, computer science/IT, supply chain management and business/commercial fields.


• **GPA:** not published anywhere. Enterprise requires a transcript up front, so grades are visible, but no minimum is stated.


• **Work authorization / visa sponsorship:** not published. The internship page and careers pages are silent on this point.


• **Class year:** not published. Enterprise names no class-year requirement.


### Why Does Enterprise Require a Transcript Up Front?


Requiring a transcript with the initial email is unusual. Most employers ask for it later in the process, if at all. The practical implication is that grades matter to the reviewer even though no GPA floor is published. Have an official or unofficial transcript PDF ready before you write the email. If your GPA is strong, the transcript speaks for itself. If it is not, the rest of the email, especially any energy-relevant project work, matters proportionally more.


## What Skills Does Enterprise Products Partners Look For, and How Do You Build Them?


Enterprise Products does not post internships to its ATS, so no intern job description exists to analyze, not for this cycle and not for any prior cycle. The skill signal comes from the employer's own discipline taxonomy (the 34 named sub-disciplines across five focus areas) and from the single reported interview question, which is behavioral: "When was a time you had to accomplish multiple tasks simultaneously." The company names no software tool, no programming language and no specific technical skill anywhere on its internship page. What it names instead are disciplines, and the disciplines tell you what to study.

## What Is the Enterprise Products Partners Application and Interview Process Like?


The process is unusually short and unusually direct:


1. **Email your resume and transcript tocampusrecruiting@eprod.com .** That is the entire published application instruction. There is no portal, no requisition number and no confirmation flow.


2. **Do not use the Taleo job board for the internship.** Enterprise's ATS at epco.taleo.net carries only full-time corporate, field, engineering, marine and driver roles. Searching for "intern" returns 23 results and not one is an internship; the substring matches "internal."


3. **Use campus recruiting if your school hosts Enterprise.** Glassdoor data splits intern candidate channels 50/50 between recruiter outreach and campus recruiting. One accepted-offer candidate simply said: "I applied for the interview through my university."


4. **Prepare for a short, casual, behavioral interview.** One accepted-offer intern described a one-on-one conversation "fairly straightforward about school and myself in general," with an interviewer who "was very easy to talk to." Difficulty: 2/5 on Glassdoor, with a 100% positive experience rating.


5. **Expect speed.** Average intern time-to-hire is 4 days across Glassdoor reports (company average: 28 days). Once the process starts, it moves fast.


Because the entire application is one email, the quality of what you write matters more than usual. Name one of the five focus areas, name a sub-discipline inside it, and reference a relevant project or coursework. The recruiter does not have a structured application form to read; they have your email.

## How Do You Stand Out When the Application Is a Single Email?


Three things, all executable before this email goes out. First, name a focus area and a sub-discipline. Enterprise publishes 34 named sub-disciplines, and writing "I am interested in Pipeline Systems Planning within your Engineering track" is more specific than 95% of the cold emails in that mailbox. Second, know what midstream actually is and be able to say it in one sentence: Enterprise gathers, processes, transports, stores and exports energy products between producers and consumers. Candidates who conflate it with an oil producer or a refiner mark themselves out immediately. Third, have a fact from the business. 14.7 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, more than 50,000 miles of pipeline, record $1.8 billion quarterly net income. Any one of these, used naturally, shows you read the earnings release rather than the Wikipedia summary.

## FAQ


### Can I still apply for a summer 2026 Enterprise Products internship?


No. The summer 2026 class has already started. The email channel at campusrecruiting@eprod.com is permanently open, so send your resume and transcript now for Summer 2027 consideration. There is no posting to wait for.


### How do I apply for an Enterprise Products internship?


By email. The company's internship page gives exactly one instruction: email your resume and transcript to campusrecruiting@eprod.com. There is no online application, no requisition and no apply button. Searching Enterprise's job board for intern returns 23 results, none of which is an internship.


### How much do Enterprise Products interns earn?


Enterprise says the internships are paid but publishes no rate. Indeed shows an intern average of $28.52 per hour, but states plainly that this is estimated from 7 past and present job postings, a machine estimate from ads rather than employee-reported pay. What is more reliable is the direction: pay and benefits is the highest-rated intern category on Indeed at 3.9 out of 5.


### What areas can I intern in at Enterprise Products?


Five focus areas: Accounting and Risk Control (including volume accounting and derivative accounting), Commercial and Distribution, Engineering (process, project, asset integrity, pipeline systems planning and more), Information Technology (including big data services), and Supply Chain (procurement, logistics, strategic sourcing, fleet management). Name one in your email.


### What is the Enterprise Products internship interview like?


Short, casual and behavioral. A candidate who accepted an offer described a one-on-one conversation that was fairly straightforward about school and themselves. Glassdoor rates the intern interview 2 out of 5 for difficulty with a 100 percent positive experience rating and an average of four days from interview to hire.


### Is Enterprise Products the same as Enterprise Rent-A-Car?


No. Enterprise Products Partners L.P. (NYSE: EPD) is a Houston midstream energy partnership. Enterprise Mobility is the rental-car company. They are entirely unrelated, and the two are frequently confused in job searches.


### Does Enterprise Products sponsor visas for interns?


Enterprise publishes no statement on visa sponsorship for interns. The internship page and careers pages are silent on this point. Ask campusrecruiting@eprod.com directly.
